title: `BETWEEN .03 AND .06` is parsed as identifiers instead of keywords
spec:
This is the sqlparse library (Python 3, no dependencies). Run the tests with `PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests`.

A keyword followed by a number written without a leading zero is turned into a name.

```python
import sqlparse
p = sqlparse.parse('a BETWEEN .03 AND .06')[0]
[(t.ttype, t.value) for t in p.flatten() if not t.is_whitespace]
```
Expected: `[(Token.Name, 'a'), (Token.Keyword, 'BETWEEN'), (Token.Literal.Number.Float, '.03'), (Token.Keyword, 'AND'), (Token.Literal.Number.Float, '.06')]`
Actual: `BETWEEN` and `AND` come out as `Token.Name`, and `p.tokens` groups them into identifiers `'a BETWEEN'` and `'.03 AND'`.

Lower case (`a between .03 and .06`) behaves the same. A word followed by `.` and then a digit is not a qualified name: the keyword must stay a keyword and `.03` / `.06` must stay standalone float tokens. Real member access such as `select foo.bar`, `select foo . bar` and `select a.b.c` must still be grouped into an `Identifier`.
acceptance: In `a BETWEEN .03 AND .06` (any case) BETWEEN and AND are keywords and `.03`, `.06` are float tokens
Dotted names with or without spaces around the dot are still grouped as identifiers
Regression tests are added and the full test suite passes
